chapters.title: Cyrus lets the exiles return
chapters.summary: God stirs the heart of Cyrus king of Persia to let the Jews return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple. He returns the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar took.

chapters.title: Those who returned
chapters.summary: A list of the families, priests, Levites and others who returned with Zerubbabel, and the gifts they gave for rebuilding God's house.

chapters.title: The foundation laid
chapters.summary: The returned exiles rebuild the altar and lay the temple's foundation. Some shout for joy and older people who saw the first temple weep aloud.

chapters.title: Opposition
chapters.summary: Neighboring peoples discourage the builders and write to the Persian king accusing Jerusalem of rebellion, and the work stops.

chapters.title: Building begins again
chapters.summary: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah encourage the people, and they resume building. The governor writes to King Darius to check their permission.

chapters.title: The temple completed
chapters.summary: Darius finds Cyrus' decree and orders the work to be supported. The temple is finished and dedicated with joy, and Passover is kept.

chapters.title: Ezra comes to Jerusalem
chapters.summary: Ezra, a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, travels to Jerusalem with the king's support. He had set his heart to study, do and teach God's law.

chapters.title: The journey
chapters.summary: Ezra gathers returning families and proclaims a fast for safe travel, ashamed to ask the king for soldiers. God protects them on the way.

chapters.title: Ezra's prayer of confession
chapters.summary: Ezra learns that many have married into the surrounding peoples and their practices. He tears his clothes and confesses the people's sin before God.

chapters.title: The people respond
chapters.summary: The people weep and agree to put away foreign marriages. A list of those involved closes the book.
